messages:
elaine (finance): Heads-up: on 2026-07-15 we will roll out two billing policy changes: (A) graduated overage smoothing (a 3-tier grace smoothing window for sustained bursts) and (B) sunsetting the legacy unlimited trial credit for new signups replaced by a time-limited starter credit pool. Goal: reduce surprise invoices and simplify forecasting. Dry-run telemetry starts 2026-06-20.

tom (product): Short explanation for customers: were introducing a short-lived smoothing buffer so short spikes don't instantly create overage events, and we're standardizing the trial to a fixed starter credit amount rather than unlimited testing. This helps ops and predictability.

henry (eng-infra): Implementation detail: smoothing is enforced at the route-level as a leaky-bucket that keeps a 15m rolling window and applies a graduated multiplier (0.5x for minute-level bursts, 0.8x for sustained 1h spikes, 1x beyond 6h). We'll expose per-tenant smoothing_state in the usage API and add headers: X-Redwood-Smoothing: active|dry-run and X-Redwood-Smoothing-Mode: tier1|tier2|tier3.

henry (eng-infra): Note: this is not free tokens. It only postpones or smooths billing recognition. Accounting will still reconcile at period boundaries and any deferred usage will roll into next invoice if beyond thresholds.

elaine (finance): Correct. From an invoicing perspective: during dry-run (6/20-7/14) we emit metrics and an advisory column on CSV exports: smoothing_adjusted_tokens (will be zero during dry-run?). After go-live we'll emit two amounts: reported_tokens and billing_tokens. Billing_tokens is what will be used for invoicing.

zara (support): CS FAQ draft: Q: "Will this reduce my bill?" A: "Not automatically. The smoothing buffer reduces billing volatility and can prevent short spikes from becoming overage hits, but sustained high usage remains billable." Also: add troubleshooting steps: check usage API, look for X-Redwood-Smoothing response headers, check Console banner.

kevin (growth): For AEs and onboarding: new starter credit = $150 equivalent, valid 45 days, automatically applied for new accounts created after 2026-07-15. Please update trial docs and the sign-up flow copy. We should offer a one-click trial-top-up for qualifying startups via the console.

elaine (finance): Action for billing ops: review invoice templates for the new fields (billing_tokens, smoothing_note) and confirm tax/tier calculations unchanged. We'll run parallel invoices for 2 billing cycles for a random subset.

henry (eng-infra): Dev checklist: feature flag name: smoothing_route_window. We'll ship dry-run toggles enabled org-wide but non-billable until 7/15. Usage API addition: /v1/usage?include_smoothing=true returns smoothing_state and effective_tokens. We'll log a metric smoothing.applied with tag mode=tier1|tier2|tier3.

zara (support): Can we get a short email script for customers who see a usage dip or shifted invoice? e.g., "We deployed a smoothing buffer; you might see some usage shifted to the next invoice. No action needed; contact us if numbers look off."

tom (product): Yes, we'll put a banner + in-console explainer and ship an email template. Also adding a note to the change log and status page for the rollout date.

ops-bot: scheduled task created: "smoothing-dryrun-metrics-collection" start=2026-06-20T00:00:00Z owner=eng-infra :white_check_mark:

elaine (finance): Key risks: confusion from customers who have automated reconciliation and expect exact per-token parity. Mitigation: 1) 4-week notice + email; 2) CSV column mapping guide; 3) sample reconciliations for top 20 customers.

kevin (growth): Marketing to draft a short blog post focusing on stability and predictability, not cost-saving promises. Draft due 2026-06-10.

henry (eng-infra): Rolling out staging dry-run tomorrow. I will post rollout notes and an opt-out toggle for early-access tenants.

elaine (finance): Thanks everyone. Owners: finance (elaine) owns invoicing templates and reconciliation plan; infra (henry) owns feature flag and usage API; support (zara) owns CS scripts; product (tom) owns announcements; growth (kevin) owns signup copy. Please update the playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/overage-smoothing (internal).

zara (support): Copy that. Will prepare canned replies and a triage sheet.

tom (product): Final note: this is a policy change with product impact. Expect sales enablement and a short all-hands blurb next week.
